caption: The site as it was: a headline, three lines of CV, Inter. Fine, and untouched for two years.
Rebuilt as one editable text file. My caret types the first line, then pastes the rest.
Typed out every line, fumbling my own name along the way. It felt alive, and took a minute.
A minute is a long time on a homepage. Only the homepage types now, and faster.
Your edits survive a refresh, and the page only types itself once.
Every line on one rhythm, with no extra gaps between items. It reads like a text file.
Tried fading letters in behind the caret to hide the choppiness. It looked bad, so I cut it and made the rhythm perfectly even instead.
Watching the whole page type got old by the third visit. Now only the hello is typed, and the rest settles in line by line.
Words kept jumping to the next line mid-word. Now the text is there from the start, invisible, and typing just reveals it.
Two people on one page. I tried a name tag, a pin head and dots, and ended up with two plain carets in different colours.
Tighter letter spacing, a 1.6 line height, and 62px between sections: the line height × φ.
Canned replies to every edit felt like a dim chatbot. Now there's one honest note, and after that my caret just looks.
My caret steps aside when you come close, follows you down the page, and says hi! when you hover over it.
Product-style buttons, a proper back button, and my note in my colour.
Recorded myself typing the header so it has my real rhythm, typo and all. The rest of the page now builds in while I'm still typing.
